DuplicationPercent.note: Picard MarkDuplicates on each replicate's merged library, before filtering: the only MarkDuplicates table in the release's MultiQC config with no anchor, so MultiQC 1.13 writes it as multiqc_picard_dups (.yaml, from the config's data_format: yaml), rows named <sample>_REP<n> after the config's extra_fn_clean_exts. The table keeps Picard's 0-1 fraction, so $derived.duplication_pct multiplies it by 100. A replicate sequenced over several runs is a multi-run sample and gets no backfill. The merged-replicate MarkDuplicates table MultiQC writes under its own anchor (mrep_picard) is not read: its rows are the replicate groups, which have no D.SEQ of their own. Table name, row names and the fraction are unverified until a real run

deliberately_unmapped.why: Picard's 0-1 fraction; DuplicationPercent reads it as a percentage through $derived.duplication_pct.
Picard's library name (the read group's LB), not a measurement.

unmapped_files.why: FastQC reports on the raw reads; QC, not a result of the analysis.
Trim Galore logs, FastQC of the trimmed reads, and the trimmed reads themselves (with --save_trimmed): an intermediate of the registered alignment.
Library-level alignments (with --save_align_intermeds), their samtools stats, STAR logs and unmapped reads (with --save_unaligned): intermediates of the merged-library BAM the aln rule registers.
Merged, duplicate-marked and pre-orphan-removal BAMs (with --save_align_intermeds): earlier states of the filtered clN BAM the aln rule registers.
The orphan-removed alignment before sorting (with --save_align_intermeds): the same reads as the sorted clN BAM the aln rule registers.
samtools, Picard and Preseq QC of the merged alignments; summarised in the MultiQC report.
samtools and Picard QC of the merged-replicate alignments; summarised in the MultiQC report.
deepTools plotFingerprint and plotProfile QC (enrichment and TSS profiles): plotted in the MultiQC report, not a sample result.
ataqv's per-sample ATAC-seq QC JSON and its HTML viewer: QC; its TSS enrichment has no attribute yet and is listed for the owner.
MACS2's peak table and gapped peaks: the same calls as the narrowPeak or broadPeak file the peaks rules register.
MACS2 summits (narrow mode): one point per registered peak, derived from the same call.

HOMER peak-to-gene annotation of the registered peaks (and of the consensus set): an annotation a user can rebuild from the registered files, and a peak row's one secondary slot is kept for its own losing variant (G-4).
MACS2 and HOMER QC plots and the FRiP, peak-count and annotation MultiQC custom-content files: QC read through MultiQC.
The consensus peak set again as SAF and as presence/absence spreadsheets, and its UpSetR intersection files: reformats of the consensus BED the consensus rule registers.
atacseq's DESeq2 step is QC only: PCA, sample distances and the vst DESeqDataSet over the consensus counts, with no contrast. No differential result exists to register.
The same QC-only DESeq2 step over the merged-replicate consensus counts: PCA and sample distances, with no contrast.
IGV session file and its file list: points at the registered files, holds no data of its own.
Reference FASTA, blacklist, gene BED and aligner indexes (with --save_reference): reference files, not sample data.
